title: Recent work and hopes for Dixieland
summary: Herbert Leary, Albert French, leading the band at the Paddock Lounge, and his view of Dixieland versus rock and roll.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: And... After playing with the Four Tones, I began to...we broke up. And I played just as I would be called. Then I later joined Herbert Leary's Orchestra. And I played with him up until now. And about a year and a half ago, I came in charge of the band at the Paddock Lounge. That's how I got to Dixieland Group. And I played with Albert French's office. He has a tuxedo band. I played with him on the out-of-town engagements because his bass players sometimes can't get away from work.
Yes, he told me that. And I'm hoping I'd catch you sometime with him, but I didn't... Yes. And now you have your own group down there on St. Peter's Street at Haysha. So, this is really a nice group.

Thank you very much. I would like to see that group develop because... I feel that the Dixieland music has great potential now. There was such a change in the trend of music when rock and roll came in. I'm not speaking against rock and roll because... It fills the place. It has a good picture. It has its merit. It definitely has its merit. But, it had gone so far away from the real music until something had to come back and bring it back to its normalcy. And I think that Dixieland is about the only thing that can do it. That's why I would like, if such as possible, to have my group develop. We are playing down there, as you know, on the 7th again.
Yeah, on December. And I hope that you'll be there to hear it.
